---
title: "Self-check: acids, bases and ionisation"
---

Answer before opening each explanation. Repair your drawing or explanation
after checking it. These are formative questions, not a formal examination.

## 1. Where does the first arrow start?

In hydroxide deprotonation of an alcohol, should an electron-flow arrow begin
at hydroxide oxygen's lone pair, at the acidic hydrogen, or at the product?

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
At the hydroxide lone pair. The arrow ends at the acidic H. A second arrow
moves the original O–H bonding pair onto the alcohol oxygen.
:::

## 2. Which charge follows proton loss?

CH₃NH₃⁺ loses H⁺. Give the formula and charge of its conjugate base.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
CH₃NH₂, neutral. Losing a positive proton reduces the net charge by one.
:::

## 3. Does the ion switch between resonance forms?

Explain the relationship between the two equivalent ethanoate contributors.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
They are representations of one delocalised ion, not two equilibrating ions.
Electron placement differs; nuclear positions and connectivity do not.
:::

## 4. At pH one unit below pKa, what is ionised?

Choose 9.1%, 10%, 50% or 90.9%, and show your ratio-to-fraction conversion.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
The ratio A⁻/HA is 0.1, so the fraction is 0.1/1.1, about 9.1%.
:::

## 5. Can an ionisation curve predict the isolated mass after extraction?

State at least two additional quantities you would need.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Check your answer"}
No. Partition information and phase volumes are needed, with initial amount
and any losses relevant to a mass prediction. Aqueous ionisation is only one
part of the model.
:::
